title: Rewrite decision cards to lead with a yes/no question and outcomes
summary: Rewrite each card on decisions.html (xtask/src/decisions.rs) for the owner, who must tell in five seconds what they are deciding: a plain yes/no question, one line for yes, one for no, cost and risk in a few words, and Athena's recommendation with a one-line reason. Evidence paths, record ids and the record link move into a collapsed details section. Prior job 20261103-201526-t4qv (open-and-above-limit filter) has no candidate and no findings; this change builds on the current page and does not redo that filter.

defaults_applied.how: Change is Rust in the xtask crate.
Add tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check rendered card order and text, not wiring.
Doc comments updated for an outside reader.
One file's rendering changed, no schema change.
Verifier runs cargo test and clippy and inspects rendered output.
The check is that the owner can tell the decision from the card top.
Order and jargon rules enforced by tests and Brief::check, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read xtask/src/decisions.rs (entry: write -> render(&locate(root)); locate resolves the records branch tip via athena_git::records_branch::resolve_tip, then read_snapshot lists records/work-items, records/work-decisions and records/roles and parses each blob with athena_data::records::check_record_file; proposals decided by a work decision are dropped; Brief::new builds a card, Brief::check refuses over MAX_WORDS=120 or no 'Recommendation:' line; Brief::html emits the card). I read crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (WorkItem has only title, rung, role, source, evidence, key; validate() requires evidence for proposals) and xtask/src/site.rs (DECISIONS_PAGE, CSS, escape, source_url). The change adds no record or data file under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are unaffected and the records validation allow-list needs no change. The property (order of lines in a card) is measured directly on the rendered HTML string of Brief::html/render by finding byte offsets of the question, yes, no, cost and recommendation lines versus the first path/record id, not through a stand-in.

Job 20261103-201526-t4qv: it was only proposed, not verified, with no candidate files and no findings. Nothing from it is kept or dropped; this job edits the same file as it exists in the snapshot, and the filter behaviour (open, above-limit only; 'Nothing waiting for you') is left to that job and not changed here.
Audience is the owner reading the published decisions page; the goal is a five-second grasp of the decision. Style rules are docs/conventions/owner-style.md.

Proposal records carry no yes/no, cost or risk fields, so the card text is derived by code from the title, rung and the raising role's recorded limit, with plain-word templates (no schema change). Cost and risk are short plain phrases chosen from the rung, labelled as Athena's estimate, never invented numbers.

The 'audience role rates a sample page' criterion is met by a test that renders a sample page and checks the owner-style rules mechanically (word limit, no jargon words), plus the existing owner-style check if one exists; no new role is created.
Jargon banned in visible text (outside the collapsed details): rung names, role names, record kinds such as work item, proposal record, blind spot, job, commit, path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a new test renders a card (Brief::html) from a sample WorkItem proposal and asserts the byte offsets of the question (ending in '?'), the 'If yes' line, the 'If no' line, the cost/risk line and the recommendation line are all smaller than the offset of the first evidence path, record id or record link.

Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test asserts the evidence list, record id and GitHub record link sit inside a collapsed `<details>` element (no `open` attribute) in the card HTML, and nothing visible outside it contains a path or record id.

Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test renders a sample page of several cards and checks owner-style rules mechanically: each card's visible words are within MAX_WORDS, the visible text contains none of the banned jargon (rung names, role names, 'work item', 'proposal', 'blind spot', 'job', 'commit', 'path'), and each card has exactly one question.
Run `cargo test -p xtask`: the recommendation line states Recommend yes or Recommend no with a one-line reason, and a card without a recommendation is still refused by Brief::check.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean; and `cargo test --workspace` passes including the existing xtask site tests that read decisions.html.
Grep xtask/src/decisions.rs: the old visible lines 'Rung:', 'Raised by:', 'Source:' no longer appear outside the details section, and the module doc comment describes the new card layout.
The diff touches no file under records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows, and adds no record or data file under crates/.

out_of_scope: Changing which proposals are listed (open, above-limit filter, 'Nothing waiting for you'): that is job 20261103-201526-t4qv.
Adding fields to WorkItem or any record schema, or any file under crates/.
athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows, records/ and prompt files.
Recording or applying decisions from the page; it stays display-only.
